page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance belonging to the Enhanced family. It runs on the KVM hypervisor and is powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core using hyper-threading on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning totals 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB allocated per thread. CPU cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 (AVX512F and AVX512_VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reflect consistent mid-tier compute capabilities paired with superior memory subsystems. In general processing tests, the server recorded a PassMark CPU score of 21,177.19 alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,636.0 and a single-core score of 1,600.0, placing overall CPU performance in the middle 50% tier. In contrast, the memory subsystem demonstrated top-tier throughput, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2,767.13 (top 25%) and uncached 256 MB read bandwidth of 101.82 GB/sec. The server processed 15.01 million Redis SET operations per second and handled small LLM (135M) text generation at 273.35 tokens per second, falling into the top 25% bracket for text generation.

Hardware tradeoffs focus strictly on memory density over storage and peripheral expansion. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains 0 GPUs, necessitating reliance on network-attached block storage for persistence. Network throughput is capped at a 6 Gbps baseline, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. From a cost efficiency perspective, allocating 128 GB of RAM over 16 vCPUs provides dense in-memory capacity without requiring purchase of excessive core counts.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.4xlarge is technically aligned with memory-intensive operational workloads. Suitable applications include in-memory key-value databases like Redis or Memcached, large-scale caching layers, enterprise relational database systems requiring substantial buffer pools, and medium-scale ETL transformations where datasets reside directly in memory.
